'''Piotr Jacek Flatau''' (born 1953) is a Polish-American [[atmospheric physics|atmospheric physicist]] and professor of physical sciences.<ref name="professor-title" /> His research concerns [[cloud physics|cloud microphysics]], [[radiative transfer]], tropical dynamics, and electromagnetic scattering. With astrophysicist [[Bruce T. Draine]], he co-developed [https://ddscat.com/ DDSCAT], a widely used implementation of the [[discrete dipole approximation]] for calculating scattering and absorption by irregular particles.<ref name="draine-flatau-1994" /><ref name="yurkin-hoekstra-2007" /> His other work includes contributions to cloud-microphysics parameterizations and research on tropical aerosols, equatorial waves, and extreme rainfall.<ref name="rams-microphysics" /><ref name="lelieveld-2002" /><ref name="latos-2021" /> He has worked at the [[Scripps Institution of Oceanography]], [[University of California, San Diego]] (UC San Diego), since
1992 and was elected a foreign member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] in 2017.<ref name="habilitation-summary" /><ref name="pan" />
Outside atmospheric science, Flatau has edited books and contributed translations and songs to theatrical and documentary projects concerning Polish scientific, literary, and interwar cultural history.<ref name="uncinus-books" /><ref name="uncinus-stage" /><ref name="uncinus-films" />
== Early life and education ==
Flatau was born in Poland in 1953. He graduated from the Tadeusz Reytan School in Warsaw in 1972.<ref name="reytan" /> In 1977 he received an MSc in [[theoretical physics]] from the Faculty of Physics at the [[University of Warsaw]], where his supervisor was {{ill|Jerzy Mycielski|pl|Jerzy Mycielski (fizyk)}}.<ref name="habilitation-summary" /><ref name="raczynski" /> He then worked as an assistant professor at the faculty's Institute of Geophysics under [[Krzysztof Edward Haman]].<ref name="malinowski-review" /><ref name="fuw-history" />
After moving to the United States in 1982, Flatau studied at [[Colorado State University]]. He received an MSc in atmospheric science in 1985 and a PhD in atmospheric science in 1992.<ref name="habilitation-summary" /><ref name="thesis" /> His doctoral dissertation, ''Scattering by irregular particles in anomalous diffraction and discrete dipole approximations'', was jointly supervised by [[William R. Cotton]] and [[Graeme Stephens]].<ref name="habilitation-summary" /><ref name="thesis" />
In 2012 Flatau received a [[habilitation]] degree in physics from the Faculty of Physics at the University of Warsaw, based on work concerning exact methods of single and multiple scattering.<ref name="polish-science" /><ref name="raczynski" />
== Career ==
Flatau joined the Climate, Atmospheric Science and Physical Oceanography division of Scripps Institution of Oceanography in 1992. At Scripps, he initially worked with [[Veerabhadran Ramanathan]] and [[Paul Crutzen]] on major climate field projects, including CEPEX, INDOEX, and MINOS.<ref name="habilitation-summary" /> He is also a member of the scientific council of the Polish climate-education website ''Nauka o Klimacie''.<ref name="climate-council" />
== Research ==
=== Discrete dipole approximation and DDSCAT ===
Flatau and Draine began developing DDSCAT in 1990 at [[Princeton University]]. The software implements the discrete dipole approximation to calculate electromagnetic scattering and absorption by targets such as ice crystals, dust, soot, and marine phytoplankton.<ref name="draine-flatau-1994" /><ref name="ddscat-website" /> Their 1994 description of the method appeared in the ''[[Journal of the Optical Society of America A]]''.<ref name="draine-flatau-1994" /> Later versions extended the method to periodic targets.<ref name="draine-flatau-2008" /> An independent review described DDSCAT as the publicly available program that helped popularize the discrete dipole approximation.<ref name="yurkin-hoekstra-2007" />
=== Cloud physics and microphysical parameterization ===
Flatau contributed to the Colorado State University Regional Atmospheric Modeling System cloud-microphysics module and, with Johannes Verlinde and William R. Cotton, derived analytical solutions for particle-collection growth used in bulk parameterizations.<ref name="rams-microphysics" /><ref name="verlinde-1990" /> The Thompson microphysics scheme for the [[Weather Research and Forecasting Model]] and [[MM5 (weather model)|MM5]] cited this work, while Jerry M. Straka's textbook drew on the RAMS module.<ref name="thompson-wrf-2006" /><ref name="straka-book" /> He also studied the radiative effects of cirrus clouds.<ref name="stephens-1990" />
Flatau also worked with the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory]] on aerosol modelling and high-resolution radar studies of clouds near the [[Kennedy Space Center]]. With Jerome M. Schmidt and colleagues, he reported radar observations of individual raindrops in the free atmosphere.<ref name="schmidt-pnas-2012" /> With Schmidt and Paul R. Harasti, he proposed "mixed-phase nimbostratus uncinus" as a separate subclass of [[nimbostratus cloud]], characterized by billow cloud structure, shallow circulation, and slanted periodic rain shafts.<ref name="schmidt-2017" />
=== Tropical dynamics ===
Flatau has studied interactions between the tropical ocean and atmosphere, including the [[Madden–Julian oscillation]], monsoon onset, equatorial waves, and tropical cyclogenesis.<ref name="flatau-1997" /><ref name="flatau-2001" /> With collaborators, he linked interactions between convectively coupled [[Kelvin wave|Kelvin]] and [[Rossby wave|equatorial Rossby waves]] to extreme rainfall and flooding in southwest [[Sulawesi]], finding that the waves' combined activity substantially increased the probability of such events.<ref name="latos-2021" />
=== Field projects ===
Flatau participated in the Central Equatorial Pacific Experiment (CEPEX) in 1993, where research he co-authored quantified the radiative effects of tropical convection, and in the 1999 [[Indian Ocean Experiment]] (INDOEX), where [[lidar]] observations characterized vertical aerosol-extinction profiles.<ref name="collins-1996" /><ref name="welton-2002" /> During the Mediterranean Intensive Oxidant Study (MINOS) on [[Crete]] in 2001, he co-authored studies of aerosol radiative forcing and long-range pollution transport over the Mediterranean.<ref name="markowicz-2002" /><ref name="lelieveld-2002" />
In the 2004 United Arab Emirates Unified Aerosol Experiment (UAE<sup>2</sup>), Flatau was principal investigator for aerosol-scattering and radiative-forcing research, and he also worked on satellite ocean-colour validation through NASA's SIMBIOS project.<ref name="uae2-report" /><ref name="markowicz-2008" /><ref name="simbios-1998" /> In 2018–2019 he was an NSF co-principal investigator for the Equatorial Line Observations
campaign, which examined equatorial Kelvin waves; related research studied meteorological drivers of floods on [[Sumatra]].<ref name="noaa-elo" /><ref name="baranowski-2020" />
== Historical and literary work ==
Flatau is a grandson of neurologist [[Edward Flatau]] and a son of physician Joanna Flatau.<ref name="lewera" />
=== Books and publishing ===
Flatau has edited books on the history of science, literature, and music.<ref name="e-isbn" /><ref name="uncinus-books" /> With Katarzyna Zimek, he edited ''{{lang|pl|Kilka wierszy Władysława Szlengla}}'' (''Several Poems by Władysław Szlengel'', 2020), a collection of prewar work by [[Władysław Szlengel]].<ref name="szlengel-book" /> His ''{{lang|pl|Edward Flatau i jego dwie córki}}'' concerns the neurologist, his family, and the beginnings of Polish neurology.<ref name="edward-amazon" />
In 2024 Flatau edited a commemorative volume about atmospheric physicist [[Krzysztof Edward Haman]].<ref name="haman-amazon" /> His ''{{lang|pl|Tango: Reportaże z przeszłości}}'' (''Tango: Reports from the Past'') traces Polish tango and its movement between continents.<ref name="uncinus-tango-book" />
=== Theatre, music, and film ===
Flatau translated [[Argentine tango]] lyrics into Polish for the 2014 musical ''Tango FM'' and for concerts by singer [[Olga Avigail Mieleszczuk]].<ref name="tango-fm" /><ref name="uncinus-stage" /><ref name="olga-tango" /> He also adapted songs for plays by Steve Hauk and Tomasz Lerski.<ref name="uncinus-stage" />
He wrote the screenplay for the 2025 documentary ''{{lang|pl|Edward Flatau i jego dwie córki}}'', contributed to the BBC Radio 3 documentary ''Tango Goes East'', and wrote the Polish popular-science blog ''Fizyka Klimatu'' from 2010 to 2016.<ref name="uncinus-films" /><ref name="bbc-tango" /><ref name="gburski" />
== Sailing and meteorology ==
Flatau was involved in sailing from his youth and later joined the Polish Yacht Club of San Francisco.<ref name="sailing-weather" /> Beginning in 2005, he and Bogumił Jakubiak provided weather forecasting assistance to Poland's [[470 (dinghy)|470-class]] sailing team. In 2006 he prepared forecasts for the Polish national team during a pre-Olympic regatta in [[Qingdao]], China.<ref name="qingdao" /> In 2011–2012 he worked as a meteorologist during Roman Paszke's attempt to sail around the world from east to west in the catamaran ''Gemini 3''.<ref name="paszke" />
== Honors and memberships ==
Flatau received the Polish state title of professor of physical sciences on 2 December 2016.<ref name="professor-title" /> In 2017 he was elected a foreign member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="pan" />
